_comment: Curated license-gate registry behind /licenses. One entry per CREDENTIAL (not per occupation — the PE gates five of our occupations), each with the issuing body's official URL, the honest path, and the occupations it gates (slugs must exist in occupations.json; per-occupation one-line labels live there and render beside each chip). CH entries lean on the SBFI reglementierte-Berufe framework and name the recognition route for foreign credentials, because that is the question a Quereinsteiger or immigrant actually has. Where a precise duration would be invented, the entry says how the time is set instead of faking a number. Grows by hand; verify the official URL before adding.

us.name: Architect registration (RA)
us.path: Accredited degree, ~3,700 documented experience hours (AXP), then the six-division ARE exam. Landscape architecture runs the parallel LARE route.
us.time: 2–5 years after the degree, set by experience hours and exam pass rates, not by skill overlap.
us.note: Only the title and the stamp are gated: unlicensed designers work in every firm, but cannot call themselves architect or sign drawings.

us.name: Professional Engineer (PE)
us.path: ABET-accredited engineering degree, FE exam, ~4 years under a licensed engineer, then the PE exam in your discipline.
us.time: Typically 4–6 years from graduation; the experience clock, not the exams, sets the floor.
us.note: Gates responsible charge — signing and sealing — not employment. Product and coordination seats hire unlicensed engineers every day; that distinction is what makes several of our routes honest.

us.name: Certified Public Accountant (CPA)
us.path: 150 semester hours of education, the four-part Uniform CPA Exam, plus 1–2 years of supervised experience depending on state.
us.time: 1–3 years alongside work for most candidates.
us.note: Required for public accounting and external audit sign-off; most corporate accounting and FP&A roles do not require it.

us.name: FINRA securities licenses (Series exams)
us.path: Sponsorship by a member firm, the SIE, then the role-specific Series exam (7, 63, 65/66...).
us.time: Weeks to months — the fastest gate on this page, because a firm sponsors you after hiring.
us.note: Only securities-touching roles need them; the licenses ride on employment rather than preceding it.

us.name: Actuarial credentials (SOA/CAS)

body.name: Society of Actuaries / Casualty Actuarial Society

us.path: A sequence of 7–10 professional exams taken while working; employers fund and schedule study time.
us.time: ASA/ACAS in ~4–7 years, fellowship beyond. The exams effectively ARE the career ladder.
us.note: No state license — but the exam sequence gates advancement as hard as any statute.

us.name: Bar admission
us.path: JD from an accredited school (3 years), the bar exam in each state of practice, character and fitness review.
us.time: 3–4 years including the degree; there is no experience-based shortcut in most states.
us.note: Paralegal and compliance routes exist without it — several of our legal-adjacent routes point exactly there.

us.name: Registered Nurse license (NCLEX-RN)
us.path: Accredited nursing degree (ADN 2 years / BSN 4 years), then the NCLEX-RN. Nurse practitioners add a graduate degree (MSN/DNP) and national certification on top.
us.time: 2–4 years to RN; +2–4 for NP. The Nurse Licensure Compact lets one license work across ~40 states.
us.note: The hardest-gated destination we track with the highest demand behind it — Swiss and US boards alike are fed by nursing shortage.

us.name: Medical license (MD/DO)
us.path: Medical school (4 years), USMLE/COMLEX steps, residency (3–7 years), state licensure.
us.time: 7–11 years post-baccalaureate. No adjacent-skill route shortens it.
us.note: The clearest case of the honesty rule: 60% skill overlap means nothing against this gate.

us.name: Physical Therapist license (NPTE)
us.path: Doctor of Physical Therapy (3 years post-bachelor), then the NPTE and state licensure.
us.time: ~3 years for the DPT if prerequisites are done.

us.name: Pharmacist license (NAPLEX)
us.path: PharmD (4 years), NAPLEX plus state law exam.
us.time: 4+ years; internship hours accrue during the degree.

us.name: Clinical mental-health licenses (LPC/LMFT/LCSW, psychologist)

body.name: State behavioral-health boards (interstate: PSYPACT for psychologists)

us.path: Master's or doctorate in the discipline, 2,000–4,000 supervised clinical hours, then the state exam. Genetic counselors run the ABGC board route.
us.time: 2–4 years post-degree for the supervised hours alone.
us.note: Non-clinical roles (research, program, care coordination) hire without the license — that is where the adjacent routes point.

us.name: Registered Dietitian (RD/RDN)
us.path: Accredited graduate degree, supervised practice (DI), the CDR exam; state licensure in most states.
us.note: 'Nutritionist' is unregulated in many states; 'dietitian' is the protected title.

us.name: State teaching certification
us.path: Bachelor's + approved preparation program + exams (Praxis in many states). Nearly every state also runs an alternative-certification route for career changers that puts you in the classroom while you certify.
us.time: Alternative routes: often one summer to provisional, 1–2 years to full. Administrators add a graduate credential.
us.note: The alternative-certification route is the single most career-changer-friendly gate in this list.

us.name: Trade licenses (electrician, plumber, HVAC)

body.name: State licensing boards; EPA for refrigerant handling

us.path: Registered apprenticeship (4–5 years, PAID from day one), then the journeyman exam. HVAC adds EPA 608. Welding runs on AWS code certifications per process.
us.time: 4–5 years to journeyman — but earning throughout, which no degree-gated route offers.
us.note: The apprenticeship model means the gate and the paycheck run concurrently. Solar installation is largely ungated (NABCEP is voluntary) — one reason it appears as a fast route.

us.name: FAA certificates (pilot, flight crew)
us.path: Commercial/ATP certificates with mandated flight hours (ATP: 1,500) for pilots; carrier-run FAA certification for flight attendants; Part 107 written exam for drone pilots.
us.time: Pilots: years and real money. Flight attendants: weeks, via the airline. Drones: a written exam.
us.note: Three gates under one regulator, from the heaviest on this page to one of the lightest.

us.name: Real-estate license
us.path: Pre-licensing coursework (60–180 hours), state exam, brokerage sponsorship.
us.time: Weeks to a few months — a light gate with a commission-only income model behind it.
us.note: Development itself is ungated; the licenses attach to brokerage and contracting activities within it.

us.name: POST certification (law enforcement)
us.path: Academy (typically 4–8 months) plus field training; hiring precedes the academy.

us.name: Paramedic license (NREMT)
us.path: EMT certification first, then a 1–2 year paramedic program and the NREMT exams.

us.name: Dental Hygienist license (RDH)

body.name: State dental boards / ADA CODA programs

us.path: Accredited dental-hygiene associate degree (its own clinical program — NOT credited by dental-assistant experience), national board + clinical exam.
us.note: The occupation that taught this site its honesty rule: assistants do not become hygienists by adjacency, only through the degree.

ch.name: Reglementierte Berufe — how Swiss gating works

body.name: SBFI (State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation)

ch.path: Switzerland keeps an official list of regulated professions. If a profession is on it, you need the Swiss credential or formal RECOGNITION of a foreign one — the SBFI routes each case to the competent authority. If it is not on the list, employers decide, and the skill gap is the only gate.
ch.time: Recognition procedures run months, and pending EU/EFTA agreements shape them; the authority for each profession sets the pace.
ch.note: A quarter of the Swiss workforce is foreign-born, so recognition-of-foreign-credentials is the license question here, in a way it rarely is in the US.

ch.name: Pflegefachperson (nursing)

body.name: Swiss Red Cross (SRK) recognition / GesBG register

ch.path: Swiss route: HF diploma or FH bachelor in nursing. Foreign diplomas need SRK recognition before practice; the NAREG register records health professionals.
ch.time: The Swiss degrees run 3 years; SRK recognition of a foreign diploma is a months-scale procedure, sometimes with compensation measures.
ch.note: The single largest occupation in our Swiss corpus (3,600+ postings) — and the Pflegeinitiative puts federal money behind retraining into it.

ch.name: Arzt/Ärztin (physician)
ch.path: Federal diploma or MEBEKO recognition (EU/EFTA diplomas recognize most smoothly), then cantonal practice permission.
ch.time: Like the US: the medical degree and specialty training set the clock, in years.

ch.name: Anwaltspatent (lawyer)

body.name: Cantonal bar authorities / Swiss Bar Association

ch.path: Swiss law degree, then a cantonal legal traineeship (usually 1–2 years) and the cantonal bar exam; the patent registers you canton by canton.
ch.note: In-house legal work is open without the patent — the gated act is representation before courts.

ch.name: Elektroinstallateur — NIV installation permit

body.name: ESTI (Federal Inspectorate for Heavy Current Installations)

ch.path: EFZ apprenticeship (4 years), and independent installation work requires an ESTI permit under the NIV ordinance, which in turn requires the higher federal diploma (eidg. Diplom) or equivalent recognition.
ch.time: 4 years to EFZ; several more to the diploma behind a full installation permit.
ch.note: Our second-largest Swiss occupation (1,300+ postings). The EFZ apprenticeship model is the Swiss version of the US journeyman route — paid throughout.

ch.name: Lehrperson (teacher)
ch.path: PH (university of teacher education) diploma, recognized across cantons via EDK. Career changers ('Quereinsteigende') have dedicated PH admission routes in most cantons amid the teacher shortage.
ch.time: Quereinstieg programs typically run 2–3 years, often part-time alongside classroom work.
ch.note: Like the US alternative certification: the most career-changer-friendly Swiss gate, and cantons actively recruit for it.

ch.name: Psychologieberufe (PsyG)
ch.path: Master's in psychology for the protected title; psychotherapy adds a federally accredited postgraduate training.
ch.time: The psychotherapy training runs ~4–6 years post-master, part-time.

ch.name: Gesundheitsberufe (GesBG: physio, dietetics, and more)
ch.path: FH bachelor in the profession (physiotherapy, nutrition and dietetics...); foreign diplomas via SRK/GesBG recognition. Medical practice assistants (MPA) run the EFZ apprenticeship route.
ch.time: 3-year degrees; recognition procedures for foreign credentials in months.

ch.name: Architekt/in — mostly NOT a protected practice
ch.path: In most cantons anyone may plan and sign buildings — unlike the US. A few cantons (Geneva, Ticino, Neuchâtel, Vaud) restrict practice to registered architects (REG A/B or equivalent).
ch.time: Where required, REG registration reviews your degree and practice record rather than setting an exam clock.
ch.note: The sharpest US–Swiss contrast on this page, and it cuts toward mobility: an architect relocating to most of Switzerland faces employer scrutiny, not a licensing board.

ch.name: Audit and fiduciary oversight
ch.path: Statutory audits require RAB-licensed auditors (expert-revisor credential via the eidg. diploma routes). General accounting is ungated; the Treuhänder/expert suisse diplomas are market expectations rather than law.
ch.time: The federal diploma routes run years part-time, employer-sponsored as in the US CPA pattern.
